author: DonaldMyTrump
body: Hey guys, I was using the support room with some of my Spanish speaking friends, when a moderator (Jess) and her friend (Spookz) both decided I didn't deserve to be there. The two insisted that I be moved out despite the fact that neither of them spoke Spanish and were therefore not able to actually address the issues being brought up there in the first place. I was then kicked twice while I was simply asking why they believed I was not fit to be in the support room. When they continued insisting, I told them fine and that I would move out of support 1 and move to support 2 so that I could still receive support. I said to them "I'll move I just need one of you to come and I would also like to know why I'm not allowed up here. Jess than banned me for 7 days. This is blantant abuse as she completely skipped over the sticky rank punishment in the guidelines ( https://avicus.net/forums/6f91bb10e ) and issued such a large ban. Jess also then deleted me on skype as to avoid responsibility for her actions. I would like to request that Jess have her ranks removed due to this abuse until she can prove herself capable of wielding such power. I would also like Spookz to receive more TS training. Thanks for your time.

title: HOLA AMIGOS

replies.author: Spoookeh
replies.body:
Hey Zac,

From my point of view, you entered the support room when you were not needed. 2 of the Spanish players poked me saying that they didn't ask you to be there or require you to be there. I asked you to leave, Jess asked you to leave then I kicked you. You then come straight back and continue abusing the room. Jess then bans you and, although it might be a bit harsh, was a worthy ban. Even after you get banned the Spanish players say thank you multiple times as you weren't needed there. If you're trying to say that you were supposed to be there it's a lie.

Also, seen as Skype is a service completely unrelated to Avicus, Jess had every right to block you; she was also busy at the time and didn't need you spam calling her.

Thanks for the appeal, this is my point of view and I'm requesting further opinions on the matter.

-UK_P1NG (Spookz)

replies.author: DonaldMyTrump
replies.body:
I'll address your points in the logical order, after which I will create my own.

1. The two Spanish players that poked you were lying, and you only asked their opinion before banning me, not before the kicks. You also received "pokes" when they were all speaking openly for the support reason.

2. Skype was only brought up to show her lack of effort in dealing with her false bans, not as an actually concrete example of her abuse/bias.

3. You can't reply to appeals so yeah, a Senior is needed.

4. You completely ignored the sticky'ing that I should have received instead jumping to kick/ban.

5. You also ignored the fact that I was complying with your wishes, I just wanted a mod to handle my concerns, and as none of you three spoke Spanish and were all useless in that support room, you were more than available to assist me.

6. In your own words the punishment was harsh. Do you believe this to be due to bias or is it a random occurrence that I seem to receive that harsh ends of punishments more often than not?

replies.author: Spoookeh
replies.body:
1. Do you have evidence for them lying? Also I asked them again afterwards and they told me you were NOT supposed to be there.

2. In my opinion she had every right to do what she wished on her Skype. If you want to talk about it this is the best place for it.

3. As far as I'm aware I can reply if I was involved.

4. We believed that after warning you verbally multiple times (around 4 or 5) that a kick was the right thing to do. I do agree that mods need more training on teamspeak but it's a rare occurrence that something like this happens as most players comply with our wishes the first time.

5. You were not complying with our wishes. You constantly moved into the room to ask instead of poking one of us and interrupting the Spanish players needs.

6. No, it's due to the lack of training mods receive on teamspeak. The training isn't really needed because things like this don't occur often.

replies.author: DonaldMyTrump
replies.body:
1. I was needed in that support room. My friend Juano, a Spanish speaking player involved in the discussion specifically asked me to come up there, as witnessed by Michael. You're wrong.

2. Again, never said she didn't? Did you read my reply?

3. To give your opinions yes, but your opinion doesn't close this appeal and therefore requesting another opinion is kinda pointless as it would be needed regardless.

4.  Never argued with the kick (even though the sticky should have come first). This appeal is for the ban. Validating one infraction doesn't make your others valid.

5. I asked you and received no response, this shows extreme negligence towards the community. I also didn't interrupt or for that matter say anything until you guys demanded I leave. You also continue to ignore the fact that I complied with your demands given that my concerns also be handled.

6. So because something doesn't happen that much mods don't need to be trained? Well according to your punishments; less that 1 percent of punishments are Aimbot. Does this mean mods don't need to know what Aimbot is as it "don't occur often"?

7. I would also like to point out that there is no rule against using a In-Use support room and that the only rule that the staff can actually accuse me of breaking is going against a moderator's instructions, which is also false since I agreed to comply with the demands as long as they also agreed to do their job.

replies.author: Spoookeh
replies.body:
I would very much like to see some evidence of the Spanish players asking you to be present at the time. 

You also spoke over the players using that room to appeal a friend of theirs. We didn't neglect you, we asked you to leave multiple time and you did not agree. You could have simply moved into the second support room and poked one of us to help you out instead of interrupting someone's appeal. You did not "comply with our demands".

Like I said before, mods do need more teamspeak training and, although there might not be a clear rule stating that you aren't allowed to be in an "In-Use support room", as a regular on ts you would have picked this up, especially after we told you 3 or 4 times when you didn't "comply with our demands".

This is all I have to say, I'll leave it up to a senior to decide the verdict of this appeal.
